<objective>
The pure, SDK-free half of the phase: find the announcement, decode the payload, parse the map, and
survive every hostile shape the spec permits.

This is where the majority of Phase 7's assurance lives, and deliberately so. `packages/engine` is
SDK-free by construction, so hundreds of hostile fixtures run under plain vitest on Node in
milliseconds, in CI, on every commit — with no Caido present. Putting the parser in the backend would
make every one of those fixtures need a fake SDK.

Purpose: MAP-01's discovery half, MAP-02's reconstruction, and the whole of MAP-05, testable at
Tier 1.
Output: `announce.ts`, `parse.ts`, `decodeBase64()`, and three spec files that assert against
`map-fixture.ts`'s id arrays in full.
</objective>

  <action>
Write the failing specs first, then the modules.

`packages/engine/src/sourcemap/announce.ts` exports `MARKERS` (a frozen two-member array holding the
current and the legacy announcement spellings) and `findAnnouncement(body: string, windowBytes:
number): { at: number; url: string } | null`. The window start is `body.length > windowBytes ?
body.length - windowBytes : 0`. Run one `lastIndexOf` per marker, keep the LATER offset that is at or
after the window start, and take the URL from the end of the marker to the next newline or to EOF
when there is none — measured: monaco's announcement has no trailing newline. Trim the result. Two
`lastIndexOf` calls, never a pattern: `REDOS_INTERRUPTIBLE = false`, `REDOS_RECOVERY = kill`, and the
kill takes the operator's project with it. Copy `admit.ts`'s prohibition header verbatim in register.

Add `decodeBase64(payload: string): string` to `packages/engine/src/decode.ts`, beside the existing
utf-8 pair rather than in a new module, so it inherits `DecodeDivergence` and that file's cross-check
idiom. It uses the `Buffer`-based primitive that performs the base64 and the UTF-8 in one correct
step. Its doc comment carries Pitfall 4's argument: the other available primitive yields one UTF-16
code unit per byte, so a comment in Spanish, an em dash or a CJK character in a recovered file comes
back mojibake, `JSON.parse` still succeeds because the corruption is inside string values, nothing
throws, and the operator reads wrong source.

`packages/engine/src/sourcemap/parse.ts` exports:
  - `B64_PREFIXES` — a frozen array of the two accepted D-04 forms.
  - `decodeInlineMap(url: string, maxBytes: number)` — returns a tagged result. For a URL matching
    neither prefix it returns the `external` tag and decodes nothing (D-01 and D-03: an external
    announcement is a counter increment and nothing else). For a matching prefix it gates on the
    ENCODED length (`payload.length > Math.ceil(maxBytes * 4 / 3) + 4`) BEFORE allocating the decoded
    buffer, then calls `decodeBase64`.
  - `parseSourceMap(json: string, limits)` — strips a leading XSSI prefix through end-of-line by
    `startsWith` and `indexOf` of a newline (never a regex), calls `JSON.parse` inside a `try`, and
    returns either an ordered list of `{ sourcesIndex, sourcesVerbatim, content }` or a REASON CODE.
    Reason codes are DefMiner-authored members of a frozen array declared in this module and are never
    a caught exception's text — `contract.ts:1354-1357` states the rule: the frontend maps each member
    to its own copy, so nothing a driver said can be interpolated into a sentence the operator reads.

For the tracer, cover only the happy path plus the size gate. The hostile matrix is task 2.
  </action>

  <behavior>
    - `sourcesContent` absent entirely → the map parsed, zero sources returned, outcome tagged as a SUCCESS with zero results, not as a failure.
    - `sourcesContent[i]` is null → index i skipped, reason `empty` recorded for that index.
    - `sourcesContent.length < sources.length` → indexes beyond the content array are skipped, and every index within it is returned.
    - `sources[i]` is null → the content is still recoverable; the verbatim value is a null, not the string "null".
    - a `sections` index map → one level iterated, sources counted across sections against the same aggregate bound.
    - a NESTED `sections` map → refused, reason `nested_sections`.
    - unsorted / overlapping sections → does not crash; the outcome is defined and asserted.
    - a section whose `map` is null → skipped, does not crash.
    - a leading `)]}'` line → stripped, the map parses.
    - JSON nested past the measured stack limits → caught `RangeError`, reason `too_deep`, no uncaught throw.
    - millions of tiny sources → refused at `SOURCE_ROWS_PER_MAP_MAX` with reason `too_many_sources`.
    - one giant `sourcesContent` entry → bounded by `MAP_MAX_BYTES` upstream; the parser does not walk it a second time.
  </behavior>

  <action>
Close the announcement scan against its boundaries and prove the no-regex property structurally
rather than by inspection.

Boundary cases, each its own `it`:
  - An announcement whose marker starts at exactly the window start is FOUND; one byte earlier is NOT.
  - A body shorter than the window: the window start clamps to 0 and the announcement is found.
  - A zero-length body returns null.
  - A body with no marker returns null, and the return is null rather than a thrown error.
  - Both markers present at different offsets: the LATER wins.
  - The monaco shape — announcement at the very end with NO trailing newline — returns the URL to EOF.
  - The babel and tfjs shapes — announcement followed by a trailing newline — return the URL to the
    newline and not past it.
  - An announcement that is NOT on the last line is NOT an announcement. This is the same defect that
    makes `corpus/composite-8mb.js` invalid JavaScript: monaco ends with an announcement and no
    trailing newline, so the next file's opening block-comment token is swallowed into that line
    comment. Any Phase 7 fixture built by concatenation hits it, and the scanner must be robust to it.
  - An announcement URL that is the empty string returns a result whose URL is empty, and the caller —
    not the scanner — decides that is not usable.

The structural no-regex proof: `announce.spec.ts` reads `announce.ts` from disk, parses it with the
TypeScript compiler, and asserts (a) the count of regular-expression literal nodes is 0, (b) the count
of `new` expressions whose callee identifier names the built-in pattern constructor is 0, and (c) a
NON-VACUITY assertion that the walk visited more than fifty nodes and found at least one
`CallExpression` — because a gate that quietly scans nothing is the same defect as a gate that quietly
matches nothing. Add the same three assertions over `parse.ts`.

Prove the assertions can fail: in a scratch edit, add a pattern literal to `announce.ts`, watch the
assertion go RED, revert, and record both observations in the SUMMARY. A check nobody has watched
failing is the same artifact as a claimed check nobody performs.

If plan 07-01's `announce_scan` measurement showed the tail-window scan is expensive (assumption A2
did not hold), add the recorded mitigation: a single `lastIndexOf` of the 16-byte substring common to
both markers, run once as a prefilter before the two full marker searches. Take this ONLY on the
probe's evidence; if A2 held, record that it was considered and not taken.
  </action>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| response body string → `findAnnouncement` | Attacker-controlled multi-megabyte string enters a scanning loop |
| base64 payload → `Buffer.from` → `JSON.parse` | Attacker-controlled bytes enter the allocator and the JSON parser |
| parsed map object → the caller | Attacker-shaped structure crosses into the pipeline |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-07-04 | Denial of service | `announce.ts` | high | mitigate | Two `lastIndexOf` calls over a bounded tail window; no pattern matching anywhere on the path; the absence proven structurally by a TypeScript-AST walk with a non-vacuity assertion, watched RED against a planted literal |
| T-07-02 | Denial of service | `parse.ts` size and count gates | high | mitigate | The ENCODED-length gate fires before the decoded buffer is allocated; `MAP_MAX_BYTES` refuses rather than truncates; `SOURCE_ROWS_PER_MAP_MAX` bounds the millions-of-tiny-sources case; every bound has a fixture at the boundary and one past it |
| T-07-03 | Denial of service | `JSON.parse` stack exhaustion | medium | mitigate | Deep nesting produces a caught `RangeError` mapped to reason `too_deep`; measured catchable every time with the host surviving all 18 probes, so catch-and-degrade is available and a pre-parse depth gate is not required |
| T-07-21 | Tampering | non-ASCII corruption in recovered source | high | mitigate | The `Buffer` base64+UTF-8 primitive is the only decode path; the spec DEMONSTRATES the divergence from the latin1 primitive on a non-ASCII fixture rather than asserting it away, because nothing throws when the corruption happens |
| T-07-10 | Information disclosure | refusal reasons crossing the boundary | medium | mitigate | REASONS, NEVER MESSAGES — a closed DefMiner-authored array with an every-reason-has-a-case gate; no caught exception's text is returned or stored |
| T-07-22 | Spoofing | an announcement not on the last line | medium | mitigate | The scanner takes the LATER offset inside the window and reads to end-of-line; the concatenation defect that invalidated `corpus/composite-8mb.js` is a named fixture |
| T-07-15 | Elevation of privilege | outbound `.map` fetch | high | mitigate | Structurally impossible here: the engine is SDK-free by construction, enforced four ways, and `outbound-prohibition.spec.ts` already walks `packages/engine/src`. An external announcement decodes nothing and returns a tag |
| T-07-SC | Tampering | npm/pip/cargo installs | high | mitigate | This plan installs nothing and adds no dependency. `pnpm knip` in the verify gate fails on an undeclared import |
</threat_model>
